[WP] What are you going to do with it when it's done?

My husband and I sat on our front porch, the oppressive summer air weighing down on us like a thick, sweltering blanket. He was a good, honest, god-fearing man, and I have never been so blessed to have anyone come into my life, not since that dance at the American Legion Hall almost forty years ago.

Most of the time, we would sit in companionable silence, watching the street we had spent virtually all of our married life on grow and decay. People run out of things to say to each other, if they talk too much. People grow distant if they talk too little. Maybe that's why we've lasted so long--some times we know when to shut up.

Next to me, my husband coughed, and I immediately tensed. Blessedly, his coughing faded and passed. Tonight would not be the night. Thank goodness. He caught my nervous grip on my chair, and smiled. A pained, tight smile on an honest face.

"You're gonna have to move on from me sometime, Nelle," he softly spoke.

I shook my head. "Don't you talk like that. Doctors can be wrong. God works--"

"--And there ain't no use denying God what he wants. And if'n he wants to call me home, I'm not going to fight that, and neither should you. Nelle, what are you going to do when..."

When you die? I wanted to scream. Instead, I finished for him. "When it's done?"

He nodded.

"Don't you be talkin' like that. Ain't no good come of talkin' like that."

He said nothing. He knew me--I didn't have a plan, for life after. Our daughter would loiter around for a week or so, when it finally did happen, and would kindly suggest that I take up with another man, or join a nursing home, or any one of a hundred horrid ideas. Our church would invite me to weekly Bible studies that I haven't been able to attend recently. Some old friend from ages back would undoubtedly suggest I travel--as if I could travel without him!

He took my hand and gave it a gentle squeeze, and I smiled. All that could wait. For now, I would cherish what we had--have.
